extracted.intended_audience: typesetters, printers, typographers, book designers, and publishers
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating and selecting typefaces and typographic settings for book/print work using a specimen sheet showing font families, sizes, weights, styles, and language/glyph coverage. The page presents concrete specimens (sample text, numerals, punctuation, accented letters, and non-Latin scripts) across sizes and variants to judge suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typeface / Font family
rubrics_metrics.description: Named type families shown (e.g., CASLON OLD STYLE, SCOTCH ROMAN, BOOKMAN OLD STYLE, CHELTENHAM, CLARENDON, PONTIAC, DELL A ROBBIA, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specimens display the family across multiple point sizes and styles so the reader can assess the overall character, weight, proportion, and suitability for body text or display. Use the family name headings and the sample text blocks to compare the aesthetic and functional differences between families.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point size
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit point-size labels accompany specimens (e.g., SIX POINT, EIGHT POINT, TEN POINT, TWELVE POINT, FOURTEEN POINT, EIGHTEEN POINT, TWENTY-FOUR POINT, THIRTY-SIX POINT, FORTY-EIGHT POINT, SIXTY POINT, SEVENTY-TWO POINT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Samples show the same phrase or line of text at many sizes to evaluate legibility, texture, and optical weight for body text, captions, and display/headline usage. Inspect numeric samples (12345, 67890) provided with each size to judge clarity of figures at that size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leaded vs Solid (line spacing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimens marked [Leaded] and [Solid] illustrate different leading/line-spacing treatments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare '[Leaded]' and '[Solid]' blocks to evaluate readability and page color differences when additional interline spacing is applied. Use leaded samples to judge comfort at small sizes or dense copy; solid samples to assess compact setting and economy of space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weight and width variants (condensed/extended/bold)
rubrics_metrics.description: Variants such as CONDENSED OLD STYLE, EXTENDED OLD STYLE, CHELTENHAM WIDE, CHELTENHAM BOLD, CHELTENHAM BOLD CONDENSED appear as distinct specimens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These demonstrate how a family behaves when condensed, expanded, or emboldened — important for headlines, tight settings, or emphasis. Use side-by-side comparisons to decide on variant for specific layout needs (narrow columns, display lines, or emphasis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Style variants (italic, bold italic, roman)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimens include italic forms and roman/regular forms (e.g., CASLON OLD STYLE ITALIC, CHELTENHAM OLD STYLE ITALIC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect italic specimens for slant, posture, and how italics relate visually to the roman face; consider coherence for emphasis, captions, and emphasis within body text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uppercase / small caps / title case usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Many specimens show all-caps display lines (e.g., 'THE FIRST TIME THAT ...', 'WHEN THOUGHTFUL GREEKS...') alongside mixed-case body samples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the appearance and readability of all-caps and title treatments at different sizes; observe optical weight and spacing in uppercase for headings and display lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiscript / language support
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-Latin script specimens are shown (PORSON GREEK, ANTIQUE GREEK, INSCRIPTION GREEK, HEBREW, NESTORIAN SYRIAC, ARABIC, ETHIOPIC) indicating script coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these blocks to verify design harmony, stroke contrast, and legibility across scripts if multilingual typesetting is required. Check that the family (or matching families) provides appropriate glyph shapes and sizes for non-Latin text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accented letters and diacritics
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections labeled 'ACCENTED LETTERS — SIX TO TWELVE POINT' show accented uppercase and lowercase letters across small sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess clarity and placement of diacritics at small sizes; ensure accents remain distinct and do not collide with neighboring glyphs. Important for languages that use diacritics frequently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures / numerals
rubrics_metrics.description: Numeric specimens and figure notes appear (e.g., 'SEVEN POINT FIGURES', repeated numeric strings '12345', '67890', '1234567890').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check numeral style (lining vs old-style figures, weight, spacing) and legibility across sizes; ensure numerals match desired text color/texture and align visually with lowercase or uppercase text for tables, page numbers, and running heads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special characters / punctuation / miscellaneous signs
rubrics_metrics.description: Blocks titled 'MISCELLANEOUS SIGNS' and 'SPECIAL CHARACTERS — ALL SIZES' list punctuation, mathematical symbols, currency signs, and other glyphs (+ - × < ± = : :: / ° ' • ? etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify the presence, design, and spacing of required symbols and punctuation for the intended publication (mathematics, technical text, multilingual punctuation). Ensure symbol style harmonizes with the chosen typeface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small-size legibility and optical correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimens present the same text at very small sizes (SIX POINT, EIGHT POINT, etc.) and include notes such as 'SIX POINT' blocks and tiny accented letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to judge how well a face renders at caption or footnote sizes, and whether optical corrections (heavier hairlines, looser spacing) are necessary for legibility in print.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display/headline treatment at large sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Large display specimens (THIRTY-SIX POINT, FORTY-EIGHT POINT, SIXTY POINT, SEVENTY-TWO POINT) show how the face performs when scaled up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate letterforms for display use: contrast, stroke endings, and spacing become more apparent at large sizes; choose faces whose details support the intended visual impact without undesirable harshness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample text selection for judging color and texture
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeated sample sentence ('When thoughtful Greeks like Polybius saw the fall of Carthage and of Corinth...') is used across families and sizes to show page color, word spacing, and rhythm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent sample text to compare overall 'color' (density and gray value) and texture of different faces and sizes; this helps decide body text weights and leading for comfortable reading.
